english.title: Conspire to commit violent disorder
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), conspired together with

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSONS..)]_
(C)_[another person]_
(D)_[other persons]_

to use or threaten unlawful violence when present together with others being three or more persons in total and the use or threat of unlawful violence and the conduct that may take place, when taken together would have been be such as would cause a person of reasonable firmness present at the scene to fear for his or her personal safety
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Law Act 1977.

english.notes:
i) This offence should be reserved for the most serious public order incidents short of riot. It will be especially appropriate where the disorder has been planned, although the violence does not have to be premeditated.
(ii) The offence should not be charged simply because three or more persons are present. Always consider the level and nature and scale of the violent incident, and consider specific assault charges.
(iii) The offence may be committed in a public or private place, but it is unlikely to be appropriate for domestic incidents.
(iv) The relevant conduct may be directed against a person/persons and / or property.
(v)The suspect(s) must have intended to use/threaten violence or have been aware that their conduct might be violent/threatening
(vi) Although at least three people must have been involved in the threats/use of violence, it is not necessary that at least three should have been charged. However, the charge must make clear that the suspect is one of at least three involved.
(vii) The extent of an individual's involvement must also help determine the charge
(viii) The incident may be of a serious nature, but not all the participants need be charged with the same public order offence. The range could perhaps be from Section 5 to violent disorder depending on the individual's level of participation.
(iv) See the CPS charging standards for this offence before preparing any charges.
